commit_message:
Bug 1999464 - Don't nuke CCWs to the debugger object r=jandem

This is an alternative to the fix in bug 1995637 and removes that change.

The debugger mostly uses its own wrappers for cross compartment pointers
between debugger and debuggee globals. These are not in the CCW map and so are
not nuked by NukeCrossCompartmentWrappers. This pointer from a Breakpoint to
its owning debugger however is a normal CCW that is in the map and so can be
affected by that operation.

The change makes it so we skip nuking CCWs to the main debugger object. This
could affect other uses of this CCW but these are not accessible from content
JS so I don't think this is a problem.

It's important not to break the link between breakpoints and their debuggers
because they are present in two linked lists which are in different realms. To
clean up properly the link needs to be intact.

This change is also covered by the original test in bug 1995637.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D273012

fix_commit_message:
Bug 2003588 - Continue to allow creation of CCWs to debugger instances after CCWs have been nuked r=jandem

It turns out that disallowing this breaks the checks in Compartment::wrap. I
don't fully understand what the implications of this are but it seems fine to
continue to allow creating these if we don't nuke them in the first place.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D275046
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 0264cf850afd on top of intro 9bd0056bb97a via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (UseAfterFree): Bug 2003588 (CVE-2026-0884) is a use-after-free in the SpiderMonkey JavaScript engine's cross-compartment wrapper (CCW) machinery, specifically around Debugger objects. A prior change (bug 1999464) made NukeCrossCompartmentWrappers() skip nuking existing CCWs that target a Debugger instance object, to preserve the link between a Breakpoint and its owning Debugger across realms/compartments (they live in two linked lists in different realms and must stay connected for cleanup). However, the corresponding gatekeeper function AllowNewWrapper(), which decides whether new CCWs may still be created into a realm/compartment whose outgoing/incoming wrappers were already nuked, was not updated with the same exception. This asymmetry breaks an invariant relied upon by Compartment::wrap(): a live CCW to a Debugger object can exist, yet attempting to create a new CCW to that same debugger realm afterward is refused, producing an inconsistent wrapper map state that can be leveraged to use freed/invalid objects (use-after-free) via typical Debugger + nukeAllCCWs()/recomputeWrappers()/gc() usage patterns. Root cause: An earlier fix (bug 1999464) special-cased NukeCrossCompartmentWrappers() to leave CCWs pointing at DebuggerInstanceObject un-nuked, but the matching AllowNewWrapper() gate (which blocks creation of new CCWs into compartments/realms already marked as nuked) was not given the same exception. This mismatch between 'existing wrapper survives' and 'new wrapper creation is still blocked' violates invariants assumed by Compartment::wrap(), leading to corrupted/incoherent wrapper state and eventually use-after-free.
